title: The bank reconciliation that would not balance
instructions:
## You review a small company's cash controls

The cash book and the bank statement disagree. One clerk receives cash, records it and reconciles the bank. Work through the evidence, record the correct double entry, and recommend the controls an accounting system should enforce.

nodes.title: The difference
nodes.text: The cash book shows GH₵48,200 at bank; the statement shows GH₵45,200.

evidence.title: Cash book (extract)
evidence.text:
Oct 3 Receipt Mensah Ltd +12,000
Oct 9 Payment Adom Supplies −7,500
Oct 15 Receipt Ofori (cash) +3,000
Oct 20 Rent −6,000
Balance per books: 48,200

evidence.title: Bank statement (extract)
evidence.text:
Oct 3 Credit Mensah Ltd 12,000
Oct 9 Debit Adom Supplies 7,500
Oct 20 Debit Rent 6,000
Balance per bank: 45,200
(No credit on or after Oct 15.)

choices.text: A timing difference that will clear
choices.feedback: The receipt was cash and ten days have passed; timing differences clear in days.

choices.text: A GH₵3,000 cash receipt was recorded in the books but never deposited at the bank
choices.feedback: Correct. The books show it; the bank never received it.
Every other item matches; the unmatched item is the cash receipt.

nodes.title: The entry
nodes.text: When the GH₵3,000 was received from the customer, the correct double entry was:

choices.feedback: Correct. Cash increases with a debit; the customer's debt decreases with a credit.
The sale was recorded with the invoice; the receipt settles the receivable.

nodes.title: The missing control
nodes.text: One clerk receives, records and reconciles. Which control principle is missing?

choices.feedback: Correct. Handling, recording and checking must be separate people.
A budget does not stop cash going astray.

nodes.title: The system
nodes.text: The company is adopting an accounting information system. Which configuration addresses the gap directly?

choices.text: Separate roles for cashier, bookkeeper and reviewer, an audit log of every entry, and a reconciliation approved by a second person
choices.feedback: Correct. Role separation and audit trails are the system form of segregation of duties.
Speed does not change who can do what.
A printout of the same person's entries proves nothing.

nodes.title: Priorities
nodes.text: Your report should recommend, in order:

choices.feedback: That treats the symptom; the gap remains.

choices.text: Segregate duties now, reconcile monthly with independent review, bank all cash daily, then pursue the amount
choices.feedback: Correct. Controls first; the loss may be larger than one receipt.
The bank account is the part that told the truth.

nodes.title: Report filed
nodes.text: Your report identifies the undeposited receipt, the correct entry and the missing segregation of duties, and specifies the roles and approvals the new system must enforce.

hints: Match each cash book line to the statement.
Receiving cash: debit Cash, credit the receivable.
Who could have caught this if three people shared the work?

checks.label: You compared the cash book with the bank statement
At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: The monthly bank reconciliation, done by someone other than the cashier, is the single control auditors ask about first in small organisations.
